events.quote: on 14 June 2024, the Group entered into a five-year $3.0 billion, sustainability-linked, secured Revolving Credit Facility, with two one-year extension options available subject to the approval of lenders, accessible by British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus, each of which has separate limits. At 31 December 2024 no amounts had been drawn under the facility.
events.summary: The Group signed a large sustainability-linked secured revolving credit facility and simultaneously extinguished its prior secured facility and British Airways' export development guarantee facilities, extending and simplifying committed liquidity.
events.title: New sustainability-linked revolving credit facility replaces older facilities

events.quote: We are investment grade with Moody’s and S&P, both of which upgraded IAG during the year.
events.summary: Both Moody's and S&P upgraded IAG during the year, leaving all group ratings investment grade and lowering the cost and improving the availability of funding.
events.title: Credit ratings upgraded to investment grade by agencies

events.quote: on 23 February 2023, the Group entered into an agreement with Globalia to purchase the remaining 80% of the share capital of Air Europa Holdings that it did not then own. The acquisition was subject to approval by the relevant competition authorities.
events.summary: The planned purchase of the remaining stake in Air Europa Holdings was terminated, with a settlement payment made, removing a large potential acquisition outlay from the credit story.
events.title: Air Europa acquisition terminated with settlement payment

events.quote: The Group continues to be impacted by reliability and performance issues with Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 and Pratt and Whitney GTF engines, which are mitigated by using replacement aircraft and invoking remedy support from the engine manufacturers.
events.summary: Continued reliability and performance problems with Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 and Pratt & Whitney GTF engines, plus aircraft delivery delays, grounded aircraft and held back capital expenditure and capacity.
events.title: Engine reliability issues and delivery delays constrain capacity

events.quote: The Irish Aviation Authority (IAA) aimed to impose a passenger cap at Dublin Airport, but Aer Lingus and other airlines legally challenged the decision. In November the High Court granted a stay on capping take-off and landing slots for the summer 2025 season, and the case has now been referred to the ECJ.
events.summary: Aer Lingus and other airlines legally challenged the Irish Aviation Authority's passenger cap at Dublin Airport and obtained a stay on slot capping, an unresolved regulatory risk to capacity at a key base.
events.title: Dublin Airport passenger cap challenged in court
